Watching people · Questioning stories
Where I started · Sales

People don't buy for the reasons brands think

Before approaching advertising, I spent time working in Sales across different products and environments.

That experience taught me something important: two people can look at the same product and see two completely different things.

Priceone sees
Convenienceanother sees
Statusanother sees
Comfortanother sees
Easesomething that makes life easier

Sales taught me to listen to those differences. Writing taught me how to turn them into stories.

Creative work is where the two meet.

About

Culture, people, and the stories in between

I watch the small, strange, and funny things people do, and turn them into ideas they recognize.

I started out writing about religion, society, and the stories people believe. Sales then showed me how differently people see the same product.

Understanding people + Finding the story + Turning it into an idea.

From my writing الهجص

How a society builds a story, believes it, and treats it as reality, until someone starts questioning it.

Spec work

Four briefs, four products

Concept, copy and scripts by Khalaf. Visuals are presentation mockups made to show each idea.

01

Tissues — تفرحك وتفرح معاك

Emotional Advertising Concept

Category
FMCG
Format
Film / Social Video
Role
Concept Development & Copywriting
Through a seller's eyes

Nobody buys a box of tissues for sad days only. It sits on the table for every moment, the happy ones included.

The idea

Tissues are usually associated with sadness, tears, and difficult moments. But tears aren't always sad. Sometimes they're the happiest part of the story.

مناديل تفرحك وتفرح معاك.

Creative thought

Take a functional product associated with an emotional moment and flip the emotion. The tissue doesn't just help with the tears. It's there for the moment behind them.

02

Sukkar — Kark Tea

Social Media Campaign

Category
F&B
Format
Social Media
Role
Copywriting & Concept Development
Through a seller's eyes

In a coffee shop, people order what they already know. A new drink has to feel familiar before it can feel new, so the brand name does the introducing.

The observation

Kark tea isn't something people usually expect to find in a coffee shop.

The idea

Use the brand name «سُكّر» to create playful Arabic wordplay around the product and make the launch feel distinctly Egyptian.

سُكّر عنده شاي كرك مش هيكدرك.هنستناكم في فرعنا تجربوه!
سُكّر عملك شاي كرك.. هيسهرك!اطلبه دلوقتي من الويبسايت.
الحلو في الكرك، مش هيزود سكرك.جربه من "سُكّر" دلوقتي.

03

Tissues — دايمًا جنبك

Emotional Advertising Concept

Category
FMCG
Format
Film / Social Video
Role
Concept Development & Copywriting
Through a seller's eyes

People don't remember the tissue. They remember what was there when they needed it.

The idea

Sometimes comfort doesn't come as a person. Sometimes it's simply something that's there.

دايمًا جنبك.

Creative thought

Turn the physical presence of the product into an emotional metaphor. The tissue doesn't talk. It doesn't solve anything. It simply stays.

04

Nova — Keep Living

TVC / Social Video

Category
Beverage
Format
TVC / Social Film
Role
Concept Development & Scriptwriting
Through a seller's eyes

Water doesn't lose to other drinks. It loses to being busy.

Insight

The employee is constantly interrupted during the workday. Even something as simple as drinking can become another task when everything else needs attention. Nova makes drinking water easier, so you can keep living.

Concept

Nova — Keep Living. Don't let the little things stop you.

The way I think

Dig under the benefit

Sometimes a product doesn't have a clear personality yet. The job is to find one.

The benefit is what's printed on the box. I keep digging through six questions until I hit the story. Pick a product from this portfolio and watch it go down.

  1. 0 m · On the box

    Soft. Absorbs tears.

  2. 1 m · What do people actually feel?

    A mother at her daughter's wedding feels proud and heartbroken at the same time.

  3. 2 m · What do they do without thinking?

    Reach for the box before the tears even fall.

  4. 3 m · What do they say?

    «أنا مش بعيط.. دي دموع الفرحة»

  5. 4 m · What makes them laugh?

    Crying and dancing within the same five minutes.

  6. 5 m · What makes them care?

    Being there for their kids' biggest moments.

  7. Bottom · The story inside the product

    The tissue is there for the moment behind the tears.

    مناديل تفرحك وتفرح معاك.

Where an idea starts

Every idea in this portfolio started small.

A wordسُكّرA brand name that already rhymes with the product. A habitReaching in the darkThe hand that finds the tissue pack without looking. A contradictionCrying at a happy weddingTears that mean the opposite of sadness. A jokeTied up to take a sipThe simplest need becoming the hardest task of the day. A cultural referenceThe wedding mandeelThe tissue that wiped her tears becomes the one she dances with.
